title: Apollo 11 - CSM Columbia
_comment: Mission profile. Timeline values are Apollo 11 figures rounded [published]. The Moon and the Sun are JPL's for the mission's dates (moon.ephemeris, from tools/ephemeris/fit_ephemeris.py); a moon block of inclination_deg, raan_deg, phase0_deg and sun_phase_deg flies the circular model instead. Distances in km, times in GET seconds.

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 11's orbit at insertion, from the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-506 (Table 4-5): inclination 32.521 deg and descending node 123.088 deg east of the launch meridian at liftoff, insertion at 32.672 N 52.694 W, 191.1 km [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The report's 186.0 x 183.2 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, the orientation the CMC's IMU was released at liftoff: X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.058 deg, the flight evaluation report's), Z down along Launch Complex 39A's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The parking_orbit and translunar_coast start phases start aligned to it

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,391,607 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.97696, in the plane of inclination 31.383 deg and descending node 121.847 deg (AS-506 flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Table 10-6: the postflight trajectory at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal, the J-2's thrust decay having added 4 m/s to the C3 of -1,487,528 at the signal, Table 4-2) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. C3 is the two-body V2 - 2mu/R (ibid.), as Sivb.energy_of() reckons it. The RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for the free return the flown TLI left the stack on, past the Moon 896.3 nmi up at 75:05:21, where the preflight plan had 718.9 nmi (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, Table 7-III and section 7.4.1) [published], keeping the conic's plane and perigee; its energy comes out within the metre a second the report's trajectory solutions spread (ibid., section 4.3.4). The midcourse correction then aims at pericynthion_alt_km over the landing site, at pericynthion_get, where Apollo 11's first left it (61.5 nmi at 75:53:35, ibid., Table 7-III) [published]

lunar_orbit._comment: Apollo 11's lunar orbit after LOI-2, above the landing site's radius (the mission report's datum): targeted 65.7 by 53.7 nmi, noncircular, for the Moon's field to round it toward 60 nmi by the rendezvous (the RTCC's R2 model said 59.9 by 59.3 at 126 h; the orbit was 62.4 by 56.6), and achieved 65.7 by 53.8 with its pericynthion at about 80 deg W, LOI-2 cutting off at 80:11:54 [published: Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, sections 7.4.4 and 7.7]. The lunar_orbit start phase starts there, on the flown timeline; LOI-2's PAD targets it

doi._comment: Descent orbit insertion: the LM's pericynthion at 50,000 ft [published], where powered descent begins, on the pass that lands at the landing time

landing._comment: Apollo 11's landing site and landing time, 102:45:40 GET [published]. The site's height is the terrain's there (data/terrain/). The lunar_surface and lunar_ascent start phases leave the descent stage the propellant the simulator's automatic landing leaves (tests/scenarios/test_landing.gd) [estimated]

pdi._comment: The LM state vector the ground uplinks with the PDI PAD is off by this much at PDI, in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down): the LGC thinks Eagle is 250 m farther along, 150 m to the right and 900 m higher [estimated]

ascent._comment: The RTCC times the liftoff for the CSM to lead the LM by this angle at insertion: the lead that, flying Apollo 11's coelliptic sequence (CSI at the first apolune, circularizing 15 nmi below the CSM; TPI at 26.6 deg elevation), puts TPI where it was flown, 2 h 35 min after insertion (124:29:17 to 127:03:52 GET [published]) [estimated]

rendezvous._comment: The coelliptic sequence: CSI at the LM's first apolune; TPI 2 h 35 min after insertion, as Apollo 11 flew it (124:29:17 to 127:03:52 GET), and the midcourse corrections 15 and 30 min after TPI (Apollo 11: 14 min 39 s and 29 min 39 s) [published]. The CSM state vector the ground uplinks with the CSI PAD is off by MSFN's tracking error, LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down) [estimated]; the rendezvous radar's marks take it out

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, and MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink. A checkpoint carries the forces and where the draws have got to

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the CSM state vector the RTCC plans the CSM's PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the CSM's orbit is about [estimated]

lunar_timeline._comment: Mission Control from undocking to TEI. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get'), or 's' seconds 'after' a mission event or 'before' a time the ground has planned (doi_tig, pdi_tig, liftoff_tig, csi_tig, tei_tig), if its condition ('when') holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'). A PAD with 'near' takes the opportunity nearest that GET, and none is uplinked while the last of its kind is still to be flown. The DOI PAD follows an undocking within 6 h of the landing time. The times and calls are Apollo 11's [published: the Apollo 11 Flight and Lunar Surface Journals: undocking 100:12:03, DOI PAD 100:20:32, GO for DOI 101:17:53 with DOI at 101:36:14, GO for powered descent 102:28:08 with PDI at 102:33:05, touchdown 102:45:40, STAY for T2 102:51:45 and T3 104:21:16, liftoff 124:22:00, GO for CSI 125:06:47 with CSI at 125:19:35, docking 128:03:00, GO for jettison 130:07:49, TEI PADs 134:01:16, TEI 135:23:42], except the entries marked estimated. The LM start phases undock at 'undocking_get'

entries.say: Eagle, Houston. You're GO for undocking.
Eagle, Houston. You are GO for DOI.
Eagle, Houston. If you read, you're GO for powered descent.
Tranquility Base, Houston. You are STAY for T2.
Tranquility Base, Houston. You are STAY for T3.

entries._estimated: the PAD's time, two hours before the liftoff

entries.say: Eagle, Houston. You're cleared for takeoff.
Eagle, Houston. We're GO for CSI.
Columbia, Houston. You're GO for jettison.
